name: PDURATION
description: PDURATION returns the number of periods needed for an investment to grow from a present value to a future value at a constant rate.
tldr: Calculates the number of periods required for an investment to reach a specified value.

basicExample.explanation: At 7% annual interest, it takes about 10.24 years for $10,000 to double to $20,000.

advancedExamples.title: Months to reach a savings goal
advancedExamples.description: Months for $5,000 to grow to $6,000 at 6% annual interest
advancedExamples.explanation: It takes about 37 months to reach the goal.

howItWorks: PDURATION uses the formula ln(fv / pv) / ln(1 + rate) to find the number of periods. It is a simpler way to solve for time in the compound-interest formula.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Result is in the same unit as the rate (years, months, etc.).
Does not include contributions or withdrawals.

commonErrors.cause: Rate is zero or negative, or pv and fv have different signs.
commonErrors.fix: Use a positive rate and ensure fv > pv for growth.

commonErrors.cause: Annual rate was used but result interpreted as months.
commonErrors.fix: Use a rate that matches the desired period unit.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: PDURATION works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between PDURATION and NPER?
faq.answer: PDURATION is for lump-sum growth. NPER is for annuities with periodic payments.

faq.question: Can PDURATION handle negative growth?
faq.answer: No, it requires fv > pv and positive rate.
